feat(core+cli+mcp): S+5a — flyway_propose + proposal responses (Session A)

Flagship sender wired end-to-end. Two independent murmurations can now
run a full S3 §IV.1.9–1.10 consent cycle: tension → proposal(driver) →
object → proposal(draft) → object → proposal(refinement) → accept,
with every step signed under its kind-specific domain, every antecedent
verified per ADR-0009, and every response carrying refs that resolve
to a real prior signal in the recipient's outbox.

Core
- createProposal({ from, to, body, signer, tensionAntecedent?,
  proposalAntecedent? }): discriminated body for directive / project /
  agreement types. type='agreement' validates against
  FLYWAY_AGREEMENT_SCHEMA (sender + recipient must appear in
  participants, schemaVersion match, decisionRule enum, all 11
  required fields). Stage validation enforces driver →
  [driver/requirements/draft/final], requirements → [requirements/
  draft/refinement/final], draft → [draft/refinement/final],
  refinement → [refinement/final], final is terminal. previousStageId
  required for stage='refinement'. Refines DOMAIN_PROPOSAL. Closes #8.
- ProposalRequirement structured items required at stage='requirements'
  (id, description, mustOrShould?, rationale?). Closes #6.
- ADR-0009 antecedent verification on both tensionAntecedent and
  proposalAntecedent (kind, id, sender, DID-doc binding, signature).
- createProposalResponse({ subjectEnvelope: ProposalEnvelope, ... }):
  decisions accept/object/exit; reason required for object/exit;
  concernsToRecord first-class field (closes #3, #15). ADR-0009
  verification on prior proposal.
- FLYWAY_AGREEMENT_SCHEMA extended with optional `trigger` and
  `acceptanceCriteria` (closes #7).
- flyway_check verifyRefsResolve now handles refs.proposalId in
  addition to refs.tensionId (catches the regression the new senders
  introduced).

CLI
- runPropose loads identity, recognized-peer trust gate, resolves
  tension/proposal antecedents from outbox or inbox, loads the cached
  peer DID document, calls createProposal, writes outbox first,
  delivers to recipient inbox.
- runRespond now dispatches on subject.kind: tension subjects route
  through createTensionResponse; proposal subjects through
  createProposalResponse. Cross-flag validation: --concerns-to-record
  refused on tensions, --transfer-to refused on proposals.
- `flyway propose` verb with --type / --title / --body / --stage /
  --previous-stage-id / --promote-tension-id / --agreement-file /
  --requirements-file. `flyway respond` extended with --concern
  (repeatable).

MCP
- handleProposal: stateless; caller supplies own identity, peerDid,
  body, and optional antecedents (each as { envelope, senderDidDocument }).
  Returns signed envelope; caller persists.
- handleRespond dispatcher already routed by subject.kind; the proposal
  branch now invokes handleProposalResponse instead of returning
  not-yet-wired.

docs: accept ADR-0009 (antecedent verification before signing)

Captures the load-bearing invariant that surfaced in the architecture
review: a signer never signs an attestation over an unverified
antecedent artifact, and the verifying key is the recognition-time
cached copy — not anything freshly read from a peer-controlled path.

The rule lives in core, at the signing primitive itself, so adapters
can't skip it. createTensionResponse is the first primitive built
under this rule (S+4 + 2a2ac16). recognizePeer pre-dates the ADR
but conforms by accident. Future flyway_propose, proposal-response,
and exit will inherit the structure from their function signature.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(security+core+cli+mcp): act on architecture, TS, and security review of S+3/S+4

Three independent review agents reviewed the S+3 (flyway_tension) and
S+4 (flyway_respond) milestones. This commit implements every blocker
and important-severity finding; deferred items are noted at the end
of this message.

Security hardening (security review)
- SEC-1 (HIGH): peerCachePathSegments accepted '..', '/', '\\', NUL,
  empty segments. A peer who controls their .well-known/did.json could
  publish 'did:web:host:..:..:tmp:pwn' and coerce outbox/inbox writes
  outside the intended subtree. Now rejects any segment that is empty,
  '.', '..', or contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]. 8 new
  traversal-rejection tests in recognize.test.ts.
- SEC-2 (HIGH) / ARCH-7: createTensionResponse and runRespond verified
  the subject signature against a freshly-read peer DID document from
  <peerRepoPath>/.well-known/did.json — attacker-controllable. Subject
  verification has moved into core (see ADR-0009) and adapters now
  load the recognition-time cached copy from
  flyway/peers/<segments>/did.json. New core checks: kind match, id
  match, sender match, DID-doc binding, signature verify. 6 new tests
  in respond.test.ts including a concrete confused-deputy simulation.
- SEC-3 (MEDIUM): flyway_check now flags signals whose sentAt predates
  the peer's recognizedAt — blocks the "drop a forged signal, then
  recognize later" retroactive-validation attack. validCount tightened
  to require zero per-signal issues.
- SEC-4 (MEDIUM): writeSignalFile used a non-atomic
  existsSync→read→write sequence. Switched to writeFileSync(flag:'wx')
  + EEXIST handling — closes the TOCTOU window where two writers
  could both pass the existence check.

Structural cleanup (architecture + TS reviews)
- ARCH-2 / KIE-1+2: collectYamlFiles and findInboxSignalById lifted
  into core/signal.ts. Removes the verbatim duplication between
  core/check.ts and cli/respond.ts.
- KIE-5: getPrimaryVerificationKey helper in core/init.ts; replaces
  the duplicated `verificationMethod[0]!` non-null assertions in
  cli/tension.ts and cli/respond.ts with a descriptive error path.
- KIE-3: bin/flyway.ts now imports TENSION_DECISIONS from core, uses
  a proper `isTensionDecision` type guard, and drops the `as` cast.
- KIE-4: MCP handleRespond does a minimal shape check on
  subjectEnvelope before casting (catches missing id/from/kind/
  signature at the boundary with a useful error).
- KIE-7: TensionResponseRefs alias exported from core so MCP and core
  share the type.
- KIE-10: respond.test.ts replaces a dynamic `await import('node:fs')`
  with a static top-of-file import.
- ARCH-5: dropped the peerCachePathSegments re-export from
  cli/respond.ts (smell; callers should depend on core directly).

Documentation
- ADR-0009 committed separately documents the antecedent-verification
  invariant the review surfaced. ADR index README updated to also
  list 0007 / 0008 / 0009.

Tests: 221 passed (138 core, 9 agent, 16 mcp, 58 cli) — up from 207.
End-to-end tension→acknowledge round-trip still verifies.
